items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: So Nichole asked Sidney, 'Do you know of anybody that we could take, I got an extra ticket, that would leave an impression in Parisian audiences?' And he pointed right straight to me

ctx.x: Pete Johnson, the boogie-woogie pianist. Pete Johnson couldn't go, he couldn't get out of his contracts up in Albany, New York, and so Nichol heard the conversation because I was on the bandstand and Sidney was on the bandstand, we were getting ready to play our set, and Nichol said, 'Pete Johnson can't go. I have an extra ticket. Do you know anyone . . .' (end of Side 1)

So Nichole asked Sidney, 'Do you know of anybody that we could take, I got an extra ticket, that would leave an impression in Parisian audiences?' And he pointed right straight to me, 'Take him, he'll account for himself.' That's what Sidney Bechet told Nichole Barclay. And so I said, 'Okay.' 'Here's his ticket.'

So we played the set and after the set he wanted to talk to me and we discussed -- and here's what Sidney said, 'Chief, I don't know how much money they're going to give you, but take the job because when you go to Europe you'll be stamped -- you'll gain a lot of prestige going to Europe, especially Paris. That way I got to Paris and I have Sidney Bechet to thank. My second thanks to Sidney.
